summary.one_liner: csvlens is a command line CSV file viewer written in Rust, described as "like less but made for CSV."
summary.what_it_does: It opens a CSV file (or piped CSV data) in an interactive terminal viewer with keyboard navigation by row, column, page, or cell. It supports regex-based find with highlighting, filtering rows and filtering columns by regex, and marking rows. Columns can be frozen from the left and widths adjusted. Options include custom delimiters with auto-detection, tab-separated mode, handling files without headers, and default column, filter, or find regexes at startup. Marked rows or a selected cell's value can be printed to stdout on exit. It can also be used as a Rust library through run_csvlens and CsvlensOptions.
use_cases: view large CSV files in the terminal
filter CSV rows with a regex
search and highlight text in a CSV
pipe CSV output into an interactive viewer
pick a cell or row from a CSV and print it to stdout
embed a CSV viewer in a Rust application
notable: Interactive less-style navigation tailored to CSV, with row, column, and cell selection modes
Regex-based find, row filter, and column filter, all available as startup flags too
Can be used as a library crate (run_csvlens, CsvlensOptions) and prints selected cell or marked rows to stdout
Packaged for many platforms including Homebrew, winget, Arch, FreeBSD, NetBSD, and OpenBSD
caveats: Requires Rust 1.88.0 or newer when building from source
Library usage needs default-features = false with the clipboard feature in Cargo.toml as shown in the README
